text:
maria: hey, got a DM asking me to approve a Slack app called "Redwood OAuth Helper". never seen it before. link: https://tiny.ph/rdw-approve :thinking:
sec-bot: Automated alert: external app approval requested by user maria. App ID: A12345-EXAMPLE. Flagged: external redirect domain.
ben: @maria can you paste the exact DM content and the app scopes? do NOT click any approve buttons again.
alice: if there's a manifest or the consent screen screenshot that helps. assume phishing until proven otherwise.
maria: pasted the DM thread below, the app asked for: "read messages, post as you, access profile email, manage tokens"
---paste---
From: installer@ext-service.com
Message: "To enable faster replies for your team, please approve Redwood OAuth Helper. Click: https://tiny.ph/rdw-approve"
Scopes requested: users:read, chat:write, tokens:grant, profile:read, admin:read
---end---
ben: thanks. i'm triaging now. @ir_manager i'm going to run the approval URL through the sandbox and check the app id and manifest. ops_oncall, can you temporarily disable external app approvals org-wide until we verify? :lock:
ops_oncall: doing that now. disabling external app adds via admin console. will confirm in ~2m.
sec-bot: Sandbox result: URL redirected to bit.ly/rdw-pay -> loaded JS that POSTs to hxxp://mal.example/collect with header x-client-id:A12345-EXAMPLE. Threat pattern: credential harvesting + token exchange attempt. Verdict: malicious.
ben: confirmed malicious. containment steps: 1) revoke any tokens granted to A12345-EXAMPLE 2) block app id and domain in App Control 3) run org-wide token audit for last 48h 4) rotate any service tokens that may have been exposed. @ops_oncall please escalate to IdP/SSO team to force rotate app keys if any.
ops_oncall: revoked tokens for app id, blocked redirect domains, added domain to denylist. notified IdP.
alice: communications: recommend sending targeted message to users who received the DM with instructions to not click links and to file a report if they did. also propose a short bulletin for next all-hands on phishing trends.
maria: i did not click approve, just forwarded here. thanks for the quick action. :thumbsup:
ir_manager: good triage. next steps: 1) post incident note in #security-incident with brief timeline 2) add an automated audit rule to alert on any future external-app requests with tokens:grant or chat:write scopes 3) schedule a quick blockers review of App Approval workflow in console.
ben: i ran a quick scan across audit logs: 6 other users clicked the link and one approved the app within last 12 hours (user: rachel). reach out to rachel immediately and check token usage.
sec-bot: detected anomalous API calls from rachel's bot user: unusual mass message sends to 12 external channels. Suspended user-token pending confirmation.
ops_oncall: suspended rachel's token, preserved logs, initiated forensic capture.
ben: recommended follow-ups: - forensics run on messages sent (to see if any sensitive links were exfiltrated) - rotate org-level bots if they used the same app client id - update App Approval policy to require admin pre-approval for any app requesting tokens:grant or chat:write
alice: will own comms to impacted users. drafting notice: short, what happened, what to do (change password if you clicked, contact security), offer 1:1 help.
ir_manager: post-incident task: update onboarding docs to include how to spot malicious app install prompts. also add a weekly automated report of external app requests to security channel.
ben: adding a quick KMS-related note: check any KMS/HSM integrations that might have allowed token export—no direct evidence yet but list owners to confirm.
maria: ty all. small ask — can we get a follow-up training or short poster for the team about verifying app publishers?
alice: yes — i'll prototype a one-slide checklist and a short gif showing where to check app metadata before approving.
ben: closing notes: confirmed malicious app, tokens revoked, one compromised user isolated, denylist updated, admin approval enforced for risky scopes. I'll write a brief postmortem entry and assign actions in the tracker.
sec-bot: Note: audit rule created: alert when external_app_request AND scope in (tokens:grant, chat:write).
ir_manager: thanks everyone. after action items: review mitigation effectiveness in 72 hours and loop in comms for awareness follow-up.
maria: thanks team. appreciate the quick response. :heart:
